rejected.title: Ways to raise productivity
card: A business raises productivity when it makes more from the same inputs, or the same output from fewer inputs. Adding more hours or more workers can raise output, but not productivity on its own.
Training and equipment
Training gives workers more skill, so they work faster and make fewer errors. New equipment and technology can let each worker make more in the same time.
Research
Research can find better products and faster ways to work. A business may spend money on it now and gain higher productivity later.
Cutting waste
Methods such as just-in-time stock cut waste. The business orders materials to arrive just as they are needed, so less is stored, spoiled or left unused.
rejected.remember: Training, equipment, research and less waste all help each input make more.

a.q: A bakery wants to raise its productivity. Which change would do that?
opts: Buying an oven that bakes twice as many trays at once
Raising the price of every loaf the shop sells
Opening the shop for two extra hours each day
Hiring two more bakers to make the same loaves
a.why: A bigger oven is new equipment, so the same bakers make more bread in the same time. Opening longer is tempting because it adds output, but it adds hours too, so each hour makes no more than before.
a.clue: Which change gets more from the same workers and time?

b.q: Priya runs a bike repair shop in Hobart. She keeps few spare parts and orders each one only when a customer's repair needs it, so fewer parts sit unused or get damaged. Which method is she using?
opts: Just-in-time stock, which cuts waste
Staff training, which builds worker skill
Research, which finds new products
New technology, which speeds up each task
b.why: Ordering parts only when they are needed is just-in-time stock, and it cuts waste from unused or damaged parts. Training is tempting because it also lifts productivity, but nothing in the case involves teaching staff new skills.
b.clue: Think about when the parts are ordered.

draft.title: Ways to raise productivity
card: Productivity is the output made from the resources used, such as output per hour worked. A business raises it by making more from the same inputs, or the same output from fewer inputs.
Training and equipment
Training gives workers more skill, so they work faster and make fewer errors. New equipment and technology can let each worker make more in an hour.
Research
Research can find better products and faster ways to work. A business may spend money on it now and gain higher productivity later.
Cutting waste
Methods such as just-in-time stock cut waste. The business orders materials to arrive just as they are needed, so less is stored, spoiled or left unused.
draft.remember: Productivity rises when workers or methods get more output from the same resources.

a.q: Which change is most likely to raise a bakery's productivity?
opts: Buying a mixer so each baker makes more loaves per hour
Raising the price of every loaf sold at the shop
Opening the shop for two extra hours each day
Hiring two more bakers to make the same number of loaves
a.why: A faster mixer lets each baker make more from each hour worked, so output per hour rises. Opening longer adds hours but does not raise output per hour, which is why it is tempting but wrong.
a.clue: Look for more output from each hour or each input.

b.clue: Think about when the parts are ordered.

a.best: Buying a mixer so each baker makes more loaves per hour

a.q: A small software firm spends money on research this year, though its output has not risen yet. Why might it do this?

Research cuts the stock the firm has to store
